problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-2,1]\times [-8,8]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}y-x-1 \\ x{y}^{2}-2y+2\end{aligned}].
$$

Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts at ${x}_{0}=[1,\,1]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[0,\,4]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).

| ${x}_{2}≈[$ | {{field-1}} | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-2}} |  |  |
worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}y-x-1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}y-x-1) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{2}-2y+2) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{2}-2y+2)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}y-1 & {x}^{3} \\ {y}^{2} & 2xy-2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}y-1 & {x}^{3} \\ {y}^{2} & 2xy-2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}y-x-1 \\ x{y}^{2}-2y+2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}y-1 & {x}^{3} \\ {y}^{2} & 2xy-2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}y-x-1 \\ x{y}^{2}-2y+2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}3(0)^{2}(4)-1 & (0)^{3} \\ (4)^{2} & 2(0)(4)-2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}(0)^{3}(4)-0-1 \\ (0)(4)^{2}-2(4)+2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 16 & -2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{(-1)\cdot (-2)-0\cdot 16}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ -16 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 22\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 11\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
